title: Maple-Cured Salmon Plank
shortDescription: Cedar-planked salmon with maple glaze for ten on the grill
subtitle: Cedar-planked salmon with maple glaze for ten on the grill
description: Salmon fillets get a quick maple-brine, then grill on cedar planks until edges caramelize and centers stay moist. Flake onto platters with lemon-dill yogurt and roasted asparagus.

steps.title: Brine the salmon
steps.instruction: Dissolve salt in cold water with maple syrup. Submerge salmon 30–60 minutes, then pat completely dry.

steps.title: Soak cedar planks
steps.instruction: Submerge planks in water at least 1 hour so they smolder instead of catching fire on the grill.

steps.title: Prep glaze and sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk maple syrup, brown sugar, Dijon, and soy for glaze. Mix yogurt, dill, lemon zest, and juice for sauce. Refrigerate until service.

steps.title: Grill on planks
steps.instruction: Heat grill to medium-high, about 400°F. Place salmon on planks, close lid, and grill 12–15 minutes until centers reach 125°F for medium or 140°F for well-done. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Glaze and platter
steps.instruction: Brush glaze in final 6 minutes. Rest salmon 5 minutes, flake or portion onto platters with yogurt sauce and grilled asparagus.

proTips: Keep a spray bottle near the grill—planks can flare if glaze drips.
Offer capers for crew who want a bagel-and-lox vibe without the bagels.
Save plank trim for smoking wood chips on the next BBQ night.
tonightSpread: Planked salmon with dill yogurt, grilled asparagus, and lemon wedges.
Wild rice pilaf for a plate that feels complete without heavy starches.
leftovers: Flake cold salmon into salads with the yogurt sauce as dressing.
Make salmon cakes with panko and egg for a fast lunch shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Salmon night upgrades the hall menu without feeling fussy. Plank grilling keeps fish off direct flame, reduces sticking, and delivers real smoke aroma—even on a gas grill behind the station.
mealPrepNotes: Brine fillets up to 4 hours ahead. Soak cedar planks at least 1 hour. Pat salmon dry before grilling so maple glaze caramelizes instead of steaming off.
